sources.title: Xbox Project Helix is "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC," says lead dev
sources.text: The Helix is reportedly expected to launch in 2028 Jason Ronald – vice president of Xbox's gaming devices and ecosystem team – has spoken in more detail about what Project Helix actually is. Namely, it doesn't sound like it's a Steam Machine. To celebrate the 25th anniversary since the original Xbox was released and Halo arrived in our lives (and almost 26 since The Rock revealed the console ), Microsoft has released a magazine about the platform online . While a lot of it is about the history of the console, some details about the future of Xbox are sprinkled in there, with news about future releases like Fable, and a hint that there's maybe something going on with games like Crash Bandicoot and Tony Hawk. But the most significant bit of info is some more details about what Project Helix is. Ronald – who Microsoft describes as the vice president of next generation – says "it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine – one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed," while touting its backwards compatibility capabilities, mentioning that he's "able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly." He also speaks about removing "the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games," while explaining more about what Project Helix's rumored PC connection actually is. "We're very clear on the design goal" Ronald explains, "Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games." Of course, the real question is how all-encompassing is the PC integration going to be. Presumably the Xbox Store is a sure bet, and probably Battle.net too. But the idea of having your Steam library available on console would be a pretty unassailable win for the console, but sadly I really don't see that happening in the age of Steam Machines. Xbox Project Helix console could cost as much as $1,800 and is reportedly set to launch by Christmas 2028. sources.title: Microsoft Says Of The Next Xbox: ‘Helix Is A Console Capable Of Playing PC Games’
sources.text: Microsoft has put out an online magazine to celebrate 25 years of Xbox , and unquestionably to attempt even more damage control after a gruesome year of studio closures and mass layoffs. Within all the huff and puff lies a surprise: seven pages’ coverage of Project Helix, the codename for the next Xbox console. Within this is revealed the plan for Helix to be able to play games and even progress from every previous Xbox generation, as well as removing “the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games.” So, asks the magazine and indeed us, “is Project Helix a console or a PC?” The answer is very definitively: a console. Sort of. The current generation of consoles were notably described ahead of launch as being far more like PCs in a sealed box than the traditional console designs of yore, and this appears to be something Microsoft is looking to get away from this time out. The emphasis here is on the so-called instantaneous nature of a console. Jason Ronald is Xbox’s VP of “next generation,” and is quoted saying, “When I think about what makes a console magical, it’s that it just makes my games instantly accessible and ready to play in an instant. I don’t have to worry about updating my operating system, updating drivers, configuring different settings.” Which is…a bold claim, given anyone who owns an Xbox will know about having to install the latest updates, waiting for game patches to excruciatingly slowly download without taking advantage of your 1TB ethernet connection, or that unbearable pause each time you load it up for it to fill in the dashboard. But of Project Helix, Ronald says, “it’s really designed to be the ultimate gaming machineâone that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I’m able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly,” adding, “We’re very clear on the design goal: Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games.” However, it’s hard to know just how clear this distinction is from Ronald’s very next words. “But if you’re a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it.” So it is a PC then? So confused. Other comments from Ronald include that “We don’t think the next generation is defined by 8K or 240 hertz, or some of the traditional metricsâit’s really about gameplay innovation.” He adds, “It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering, to deliver a new level of visual fidelity in more efficient and innovative ways.” Which all rather seems to be laying the ground for a machine that’s not focusing on the very latest and most expensive chipsets, but rather one that’ll take advantage of the more recent progress in upscaling and the like, perhaps to prevent the machine costing an absolute fortune? This topic isn’t ignored. Describing it as a factor “the team couldn’t have foreseen when Project Helix began,” the component crisis gets a mention. “Meeting this challenge has become a primary driver of Helix’s innovation,” says the article. Ronald is quoted once more. “It’s definitely a challenging time, but as a system and a platform designer, it’s also one of the most exciting times because we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable.” This, he says, is why there’s the focus on neural rendering, adding, “I think you’re going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you’ve seen in the last 10 years.” It’s all a lot of words to avoid pointing out that Microsoft itself is one of the primary causes of the crisis in the first place, one arm taking all the available components from the other in order to power its AI hubris. Beyond this, the piece delivers some very confusing messaging regarding Xbox’s current desperate rebranding. After a disastrous attempt to call everything from your console to your toaster “an Xbox,” the recent emphasis has been to return to the core idea of the Xbox itself, yet that message gets very lost in Microsoft’s own marketing. We’re told at once that this is all about “the Return of Xboxâthe return of a console,” and then that “Project Helix aims to take a wrecking ball to the dividers currently keeping players and their games apart,” quoting Ronald saying Helix is about “enabling [players] to experience those games wherever they choose to play. It’s about removing barriers to play, removing friction, and those arbitrary boundaries that have existed in the past.” So which is it? There are claims the new UI will adapt to whether the Xbox is being played on the living room TV, or streamed to a mobile device or a PC with mouse and keyboard. This really does sound like a confusion of previous messaging crashing into the current reverse-ferret. There’s no word one when we can expect to see Project Helix in more detail, and certainly nothing on an intended release date. It seems that Microsoft and Sony are currently playing chicken on revealing whether they’re aiming for 2027 or 2028, or perhaps even later given the tumult in the hardware industry. But at least we know it’s a console, not a PC, but also like a PC, and can be streamed to your mobile, or played on PC, and has all of the annoying complexity of PCs taken away, but also still there. sources.text: Xbox is all-in on neural rendering to keep costs down A lead developer on Xbox Project Helix says that rising hardware costs are a primary driver of the upcoming console's development. As part of the console brand's 25th anniversary, Microsoft has released a magazine about Xbox's past, present, and future . This online magazine includes an interview with Jason Ronald, vice president of next-generation console development at Microsoft and the lead for Project Helix. In this interview, he clarifies that Xbox Project Helix is "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC," rather than the other way around. Obviously, the biggest conversations about the Xbox Project Helix – and the PS6 – are cost. Hardware prices are rising thanks to the ongoing global RAM shortages brought on by AI companies who just need to let your weird uncle generate what he looks like as a Simpson to post on Facebook. The Xbox Series X|S , PS5 , and Nintendo Switch 2 have all had price increases over the past year, but Ronald says keeping the price down is a crucial motivator in the console's design. "It's definitely a challenging time," Ronald says, adding, "it’s also one of the most exciting times, because we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable." He explains the cost factor is why the team behind Project Helix is "really focused on advancements like neural rendering, because it’s an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that." Obviously AI-assisted tech was a big talking point within games before the memory crisis, but it feels like it's only going to become more prominent. Sony has been implementing QSSR frame generation tech into its PS5 games , likely in part because nobody can afford a PS5 Pro now that it's almost $1,000. And with things going like they are, it's probably going to be the norm heading forward… let's just hope Xbox puts its money where its mouth is and actually makes the Helix affordable. But given the current rumor is it's going to be $1,800, I'm not too hopeful. sources.title: The next Xbox, Project Helix, is a console and "not a PC" says Microsoft, as it clarifies that computational power isn't sole focus this time
sources.text: "It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering." Microsoft has stressed that its next-generation Xbox console, Project Helix, "is not a PC that can also play console games", but rather "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC". The company has also underlined the importance of using gen-AI-adjacent "neural rendering" technology going forwards, and a desire to remove "all the barriers of play that have historically existed" - notably in making the past generations of games playable. The details come from a Microsoft-produced Xbox magazine made available digitally yesterday , and a Helix-related feature speaking to Xbox vice president of next generation, Jason Ronald. "When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine," Ronald said, "one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games. "We're very clear on the design goal," Ronald later added. "Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customisability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it." Notably, Ronald seemed to suggest that Helix - the console, not the handheld; "Helix" refers to a couple of machines - isn't solely focused on computational grunt. Indeed, he said the next generation wasn't about hitting 8K resolutions and 240 hertz frame-rates, but instead leaning on technologies like "neural rendering" - i.e. generative-AI - and encouraging innovation. "It's about deeper immersion," Ronald said. "It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering to deliver a new level of visual fidelity in more efficient and innovative ways. It's about new kinds of games and new game experiences that we haven't been able to do before. What excites me about the future is the idea of entirely new types of games that have never been possible before, delivered through all the innovation in the silicon and the hardware and the platform that we're delivering." While referencing the global component shortage and exorbitant prices of computer hardware, he added: "This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years." Xbox boss Asha Sharma also recently talked up the importance of generative-AI-sounding technology in Xbox's future , saying "too many ideas never become games", and that "a single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations". Another key part of Xbox's Helix vision is compatibility and game preservation. "Game preservation is core to Xbox," Ronald went as far as to say. "Not only do we feel like it's the right thing for the industry, we feel a deep responsibility as one of its biggest platforms and publishers. For the first 30 years of game development, nobody really thought about game preservation when they were designing their hardware, when they were building their games." Xbox is apparently working with game-makers to ensure games can not only be played now but also 20 to 30 years into the future. The other key facet of Microsoft's push the familiar Play Anywhere mantra, whereby one game can be played across multiple devices, maintaining your game-progress as you go. This is fundamental to Microsoft's handheld-and-console Helix plan, and something we've seen the company dry-run with the Xbox ROG Ally X handheld . "It's this notion that not only does my library move with me, but my progress moves with me as well," Ronald said. "Because I fully expect that when I'm in the middle of an 80-hour RPG, if I'm 25 hours into that and I want to play it on another device, I should be able to instantly resume from where I was. Those are things that today are becoming more common, but I think in the future it's going to be a baseline expectation of all players." Ronald wouldn't be drawn on the issue of price regarding Project Helix - a recent report suggested Helix could be priced up to $1800 - referring to it only as both "a challenging time" but an "exciting one", because "we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable". Ronald also wouldn't reference a release date, though the report referenced above suggested the handheld Helix machine will release next holiday, 2027, and the console Helix machine the year after. The next generation, then, seems to be around the corner.

sources.text: GTA 6 the game is almost here, and so are the PS5 controllers. Sony and Rockstar are partnering up to release two different limited-edition GTA 6-themed PS5 DualSense controllers. One is black and one is white. The designs are relatively subtle, but they both look tasteful and appealing. They cost $84.99 each and are set to release on November 19, the same day as the game. Preorders are live now ( see at Walmart ). Read on for more info. The white version of the controller is available in limited quantities at a variety of retailers. Sony says the white one “embodies Vice City at daybreak, from its white sands and pastel skies to all its laid-back glamour.” If black is more your speed, you can get the black color varaiant. The black version is exclusive to PlayStation Direct . Sony says this one “captures the energy of Vice City’s iconic nightlife.” On both controllers, the inside of the grips have a “shimmering, color-shifting finish” that changes color as you turn the controllers in the light. Both feature a big but subtle “VI” on the touchpad, as well as textured, inset palm tree etchings in the grips. Aside from that, these are your standard DualSense controllers with all of the expected functionality: haptic feedback, adaptive triggers, a big old touch pad – the usual good stuff we all appreciate. In other news, you can preorder Grand Theft Auto VI for PS5 ahead of the November 19 launch. If you do preorder, whether in physical or digital format , you’ll be able to preload it a week ahead of launch so you’re not taking up precious time downloading when you could be playing. “Physical” copies don’t include a disk — just a download code — but they're already shipping, so you'll still have time to preload. In the meantime, you can rewatch the GTA 6 extended look as many times as you want. If you're in the market for other PS5 controllers, the Marvel's Wolverine DualSense looks pretty great as well. sources.title: Gangland Tales From the Frontline of Rockstar's Real-Life Grand Theft Auto Research
sources.text: Gregory Johnson was sitting in the back of a police car, but he wasn’t under arrest. In fact, the cops were just as nervous as him. Johnson, an experienced researcher for Rockstar, was scouting the underbelly of Los Angeles for Grand Theft Auto 5, an open-world crime game set in a fictionalized L.A. called Los Santos, which is Spanish for “The Saints.” Outside the car window, there were no saints to be found. “We were doing a ride along in East L.A., very late at night,” Johnson told IGN in a recent interview. “It's still an active gang neighborhood where stuff is going down, so I'm knowing all the signs and seeing a lot of it, and I was super nervous about it. I was like, ‘We're probably okay, but what if we're not?’” As the car pulled a corner, a whistle cried out from a nearby rooftop. Another series of whistles quickly followed, fading as they moved along a human daisy chain — an alarm system from a series of rooftop sentries to warn other gang members cops were on the prowl. With that, a couple of bikes shot down alleyways, pedalling fast to catch up before pulling up either side of the car to escort it on its patrol through the neighbourhood. The riders stared into the windows through masks. “The Mexican gangs of Los Angeles are known to be very organized,” Johnson explained. “And I quickly got to the point where I was like, I know we've got police with us. I know they're armed. The logic of the moment holds that nobody wants this to turn into any situation. They don't want to generally initiate violence with the police. We don't want violence. We're just here to get a feel for the place and maybe poke our long lenses out of the windows and shoot some pictures. “So we just got through it and ran our routes, and got everybody back to the hotel safely, but once I saw the neighborhood activate… I mean, it's amazing to see if you're going to try and duplicate it with the gameplay, right? But when you're actually in it, you're like, ‘This could go bad.’” Even that feeling is important — the dread, the worry that things could boil over at any moment — when trying to capture the essence of a city, from its decadent hilltop houses in the Hollywood Hills to its low-income neighbourhoods over the Los Angeles River. Mood is a hard thing to capture unless you’ve felt the electricity in the air yourself as fight or flight kicks in and the hairs on the back of your neck stand to attention. “I had to keep everybody cool in the group,” Johnson, a Floridian who lived most of his life in New York, remembered. “We've got a bunch of guys from Scotland and England, Ireland. Never seen anything like it. They're like, ‘Is everything okay, Greg?’ ‘Yeah, everything's fine.’ Completely lying. ‘Everything's fine, guys.’ It was somewhere between location scouting and espionage.” Johnson himself knew the streets fairly well already, but he was partly recruited not just because of what he knew, but because of who he knew. Having worked on hip-hop’s Vibe Magazine for 16 years, as well as other prestigious music mags like Source, he was already embedded in the culture. He knew the people in the music industry Rockstar was working with, and helped make introductions where he could. He had his finger pushed hard into the pulse of an ever-shifting culture. “Dan Houser had a vision for a professional research team that could easily deliver academic information,” Johnson explained. “Basically an internal form of reporting, cultural research. The role grew right as we established the department, but he had tried to get together various versions of it, and when he hired me and a couple other people around that time, I had an academic background as well as a background in hip hop journalism, and I knew the culture inside and out. We would go through tons of pop culture and various applicable subcultures. “Rockstar has represented Jamaican yardies extremely well. The mafia culture in GTA, the Yakuza culture in GTA — all of these different subcultures and themes were really rich targets for deep dives. The better the graphics got, the better the gameplay got, the better the voiceovers got — the ambient stuff, the missions — the more background information was required to distill it into these memorable, immersive gameplay experiences. We did real life research, and these broad surveys of popular culture and the popular imagination, depending on the setting of the game, the timing of the game, and the artistic and creative direction.” In his job as a researcher, Johnson brought a boots-on-the-ground style of journalism to the research trips, embedding himself in various cultures, from gangs to underground street racing meets. He was a voyeur, one of Rockstar’s documentarians, turning moves on the street into weekly reports for the internal blog, keeping plugged into whatever city the company was making a fictional recreation of, and distilling all of that into stories the writers could use as jumping off points. Some don’t make it into the games, but others showed up as radio advertisements, pretend TV shows, full character arcs, random encounters, ambient NPC chatter, and more. They found interesting characters and used parts of their personalities and personal stories to ground GTA’s fictional players in some form of truth. At one point, a smuggler came across Rockstar’s radar. This was a guy who knew the late drug lord Pablo Escobar personally and was a major player in the Cocaine Cowboys era, the Scarface days, when the Medellin Cartel trafficked white powder into Miami through the ‘70s and ‘80s. According to Johnson, some of the interviews with the smuggler likely informed the Cayo Perico heist in GTA Online. “This was one of the guys that helped the Colombians figure out their underwater submersible system, where they were, with submarines of various quality, able to bring stuff from the Colombian coast into the U.S.,” Johnson said. “That later changed. sources.title: The History of Grand Theft Auto Easter Eggs
sources.text: When you’ve got an open world as big and dense as Grand Theft Auto, you’ve got to fill it with something. Restaurants, tennis courts, hidden packages, Strangers and Freaks. All kinds of treats to reward our exploration, some buried deeper than others. From hearts and minds to signs and shrines, the inside jokes and little secrets Rockstar’s calling card tucked in every corner of the map. This is the history of Grand Theft Auto easter eggs. The top-down Grand Theft Autos are too sparse and pixelated for the kind of buried treasures that would await us in the 3D era, but easter eggs exist even in this perspective. The most famous secret of the first GTA games involves lines of chanting bald NPCs dressed in orange robes, evocative of the Hare Krishna devotees famous for descending upon travelers at airports. If you can run the entire procession down sequentially, you’re rewarded with a seemingly nonsensical shout of “GOURANGA!” The phrase, a Krishna term meaning “be happy,” became the series’ signature meme among the early fanbase and resurfaced in the first few sequels, with hidden bonuses for mowing down Elvis impersonators in GTA 2 and football hooligans in GTA: London. For a series so devoted to examining the American dream, it’s easy to forget that Grand Theft Auto is British-born. The Scottish studio that created the series and the English brothers who made it a phenomenon belong to a storied Britdev tradition of taking the mick in the margins. From the ZX Spectrum emulator Rare buried in GoldenEye to Team17’s profane cheat codes and salty rants against Amiga Power magazine, British studios excel at hiding cheeky winks within their games. DMA Design, later Rockstar North, is no exception. DMA logos are disguised among the scenery, the pager randomly rags on staffers, and director Keith Hamilton himself sends you on a mission to find “the elements of GTA.” You can unlock R-rated language by naming your character after the studio’s credited “Project Bloke.” The developers are sharing their private jokes with the players, leaving their signatures in out-of-reach places. It’s been that way since the very first easter egg: The people in the game are talking to us, but they make it hard to hear them. The developers are very present in GTA 3. The game came in hot, suffered hurried changes, and still showed a lot of its arcadey roots. The veil between the game and its inner workings is thinnest here, you can out of bounds and fly the unflyable dodo across nonexistent towns named after team members. Look to La Luna through the eyes of a sniper rifle and pull the trigger to change the size of the moon, since the devs never decided how big it should be. You had to be willing to break the game a little bit to earn your peek behind the curtain, but it wasn’t that hard to do in 2001. Rockstar anticipated our escape. If you drive up a staircase near a parking lot in Staunton Island, you can hop out and use your car to climb onto a normally inaccessible roof. A precision jump drops you in an unused back alley, where you’ll find a sign that says “You weren’t supposed to be able to get here, you know.” The devs mercifully included a ramp to get us back into the game proper rather than risking a softlock. They knew we’d be snooping around. Some developers would dummy out this kind of content once it's discovered, but Rockstar maintained it as a running gag, slapping messages in hard-to-find spots throughout the series. In GTA: Vice City, Tommy can clip through a wall near the VCN helipad to enter a room with a simple marvel pedestal, upon which rests a single egg emblazoned “Happy Easter!” You’ll find no such ovoid in GTA: San Andreas. The closest you’ll come is the Gant Bridge that connects San Fierro with Las Venturas. The visitor center below contains a display serving up fun facts about the bridge. On closer inspection the text is actually information on the structure’s internal game files, like how it’s made up of 16,000 polygons and takes up a “staggering 1.27mb of disc space.” The sign was actually updated by Grove Street Games for the Definitive Edition release. After 17 years, the bridge’s triangle count doubled, the textures increased fourfold, and the disk space increased a whopping 3,000 percent. Good thing storage has stayed so affordable! If CJ can tear himself away from the field trip exhibits and land himself on top of the southern suspension tower, he’ll find another secret scolding among the orange steel rivets: “There are no Easter Eggs up here. Go away.” Clearly anticipating you’d be crushed by the disappointment of your futile search, Rockstar eases the pain with a handy parachute to get you back on your feet. Grand Theft Auto 4 does the bit, too. And cleverly, though nothing mind-blowing for the most part. A museum placard giving out about how hard the dinosaur skeletons were to sculpt, or a warning inside of the Statue of Happiness, through a door in the base reached only by air. “No hidden content,” reads an engraving by a collision-free closed door. Walk through the illusory wall, however and you’ll encounter something far more visceral than anything that’s come before. Inside you’ll find a ladder vanishing upwards into the body of the rusted copper colossus. Reach the top and you’ll find a scaffold standing just below a huge and hideous heart. Suspended painfully from chains, its maddening beat thunders inside the internal steel chamber and it cannot die. You’re not going to fit this thing in a bunny’s basket. It’s a darker, more unsettling easter egg than any that’s come before, even if it’s apparently just a jab at Hillary Clinton, who had gone after Rockstar hard as a senator during the San Andreas Hot Coffee scandal. The Heart of Liberty City is the stuff that creepypastas are made of, legends spread in schoolyards and over IRC. The series had outgrown this style of secret by the time of GTA 5. sources.text: Or violence, or most forms of debauchery, really GTA 6 's apparent streaming rules in China effectively turn the game into a sightseeing simulator, and presumably severely restrict story playthroughs. Despite GTA 6 not actually releasing in mainland China – with many likely to import the game's Hong Kong release – Yahoo Taiwan reports (via machine translation) that Douyin (Mainland China and Hong Kong's version of TikTok) has acquired the rights to stream GTA 6 in China. This seems to have coincided with Rockstar opening a Douyin account to advertise pre-loading for the game on the platform. However, this was followed by TikTok reportedly releasing a series of guidelines for anyone keen to stream the game. While the guidelines were not released to the public, a TikTok creator has apparently revealed them by sharing a URL from a domain owned by Douyin and TikTok creator ByteDance. However, access to the document was reportedly disabled once reports about its content emerged. sources.text: Vice City is coming to NBA 2K27 as part of a massive crossover with GTA 6 . NBA 2K27's Season 3 update will arrive on November 27, and it's completely focused on GTA 6. The new update will take players to Vice City via a new park next to the city's park. The area features oddles of GTA imagery, including the Vice City blimp that has been flying around Miami in real life and a statue of Macca the Gator, a cartoon character in GTA 6 . Additionally, the season's rewards pass will also give you access to a wide variety of GTA-themed cosmetics and items, including new takeover abilities inspired by the game. As one might imagine, fans will also be able to rep the new Miami Heat jerseys that were created in collaboration with Rockstar Games. On November 18, the Miami Heat will play a real, regular-season NBA game as the Vice City Heat , complete with new jerseys and a never-before-seen court. It should be quite the spectacle, and one that you will be able to at least partially recreate in-game. Season 3 will last for seven weeks, and players can actually get in on the action without buying NBA 2K27. If you subscribe to Rockstar's subscription service, GTA+, you will be able to play NBA 2K27 for free from November 27 to January 15. Anyone who pre-orders GTA 6 on Xbox and PlayStation is entitled to a free one-month trial of GTA+, so this would be a great way to put it to use. Starting December 17, subscribers will also be able to take advantage of free GTA-themed items and bonuses in NBA 2K27. Ultimately, it seems like NBA 2K27 doesn't have to worry about fans deleting their games in the same way Madden does . This update was teased earlier this fall when NBA 2K27 was released , but 2K and Rockstar Games kept a tight lid on what would actually be featured in the update. It appears that this is one of the final marketing beats for GTA 6, as the game will officially release this week. (I know, it's as crazy for me to write as it is for you to read.) The game will have a regional rollout, meaning that folks in New Zealand will technically start playing it a day before users in the United States (unless you take advantage of some loopholes). GTA 6 is available to pre-load right now , and Rockstar has already pushed out a couple of updates , which fans will need to download before they play the game. sources.text: Arion Kurtaj, the hacker behind the 2022 leaks, hasn't been sentenced yet The hacker behind the massive GTA 6 leak of 2022 has now pleaded guilty after previously being indefinitely confined to a secure hospital. 21-year-old Arion Kurtaj had allegedly hacked Rockstar Games in a hotel room using an Amazon Fire Stick while on bail for previous crimes back in 2022. This led to an enormous amount of GTA 6 footage hitting the web well before Rockstar had even properly revealed its upcoming title – the developer later said the incident cost $5 million and "thousands of hours of staff time" to recover from . sources.text: Arion Kurtaj’s hacking antics spoiled GTA 6 and reportedly cost companies millions Arion Kurtaj, the hacker behind Grand Theft Auto 6 ' s first major leak in 2022 , just concluded a plea hearing in front of a London judge. The 21-year-old was accused of multiple counts of unauthorized operation of a computer, fraud, securing access to computer material with intent, and possession of a mobile phone while in prison. Kurtaj, who was a teenager when the crimes were committed, pleaded guilty on all counts. Kurtaj's court plea may come to a surprise to some, as the hacker was initially deemed unfit to stand trial in 2023 . After spending two years in a secure hospital, Kurtaj was reassessed in 2025 and soon moved to prison. The hacker called attention to himself while behind bars by uploading a number of photos on social media in which he mocked the authorities. The Crown Prosecution Service confirmed Kurtaj's possession of an illicit mobile phone in a press release on Monday, in which the prosecutor further detailed his case status. The hacker published 50 minutes of GTA 6 gameplay split across 90 videos in 2022, all of which depicted a game that was not yet ready for public consumption. In addition to showing standard franchise gameplay mechanics, the leak was responsible for spoiling the series' first playable female character. At the time, Kurtaj threatened to release the game's source code if GTA 6 developer Rockstar did not contact him promptly. Kurtaj's access to this supposed source code is unknown, but more recent GTA 6 leaks have raised questions about hackers still potentially having access to an apparently playable build of the game. Beyond targeting a major release, Kurtaj gained notoriety due to his hacking methods and overt circumstances. The breach was carried out using an Amazon Fire Stick connected to a hotel room television while the teenager was on bail for another offense. The hacker had reportedly used a SIM-swapping scheme to gain access to bank accounts and other sensitive information before targeting Rockstar Games. Kurtaj is associated with a larger hacking group, Lapsus$, and is accused of causing £10 million ($13.19 million) in damages. His recent court appearance detailed more antics, like an extortion attempt against Uber in which he "posted a picture of a penis as part of his attempts to force the company to pay a ransom." The BBC's report also states that Kurtaj's custody has been rocky: He is accused of physically assaulting and biting staff caring for him. "His offending was calculated and, even after being charged with serious offences, he continued to target organisations, demonstrating a persistent disregard for the harm he was causing and the law," wrote Robert Hutchinson, Specialist Prosecutor for the Crown Prosecution Service, in a press release. Kurtaj will be sentenced on Nov. 23, four days after the official launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 .

sources.text: O Xbox Game Pass é um dos serviços de assinatura de games mais democráticos da atualidade, já que é possível acessá-lo de diferentes plataformas — incluindo os próprios, consoles da Microsoft, assim como no PC, nuvem, celulares, tablets e até Smart TVs Samsung e LG com modelos de 2022 para cá. Felizmente, seu catálogo também é atualizado quase que semanalmente, trazendo inúmeras opções para os assinantes aproveitarem — e o melhor de tudo: gastando pouco em comparação às novas tendências de preços da indústria. Se veio em busca de novos jogos para jogar através do Xbox Game Pass , está no lugar certo. O serviço ganhou um reforço de peso esta semana com a chegada de cinco títulos para os assinantes aproveitarem. Confira abaixo mais informações sobre as novas aventuras! Disponível no lançamento no Xbox Game Pass, Warhammer Survivors é um jogo de ação no estilo bullet heaven, inspirado em Vampire Survivors . Com visual em pixel art, o game coloca os jogadores contra grandes hordas de inimigos, utilizando armas, habilidades e personagens inspirados no universo de Warhammer . Também disponível no lançamento no Xbox Game Pass, Tanuki: Pon’s Summer coloca os jogadores no controle de Pon, um guaxinim que precisa restaurar um santuário antes do Festival Tanuki. Para cumprir a missão, será necessário entregar encomendas de bicicleta, fazer amizades e ajudar os moradores em atividades como preparar sushi e participar de lutas de sumô. Outro game a compor o Game Pass no lançamento, Hope in the City é uma aventura de mistério protagonizada por Hope Song, uma jovem de 17 anos que descobre o desaparecimento dos pais ao voltar para casa. Durante a investigação, os jogadores precisam transformar desenhos em pistas e desvendar segredos cada vez mais misteriosos sobre a família da protagonista. Thronefall é um jogo de estratégia minimalista em que os jogadores precisam construir e administrar um reino durante o dia e protegê-lo de invasores durante a noite. Para sobreviver às ondas de inimigos, será necessário equilibrar a economia, fortalecer as defesas, recrutar soldados e participar diretamente dos combates. Por fim, em John Carpenter’s Toxic Commando , até quatro jogadores podem se unir em uma aventura cooperativa de ação e sobrevivência contra hordas de zumbis. Ambientado em um mundo tomado por criaturas, o game apresenta missões em cenários semiabertos e coloca os jogadores em uma jornada para tentar salvar a humanidade. sources.title: The latest GTA 6 leak comes in the form of a 34-song tracklist for GTA 6: The Album, featuring Dua Lipa, Lana Del Rey, Rina Sawayama, and more
sources.text: We are now just four days away from the release of GTA 6 on Xbox Series X/S and PS5, but the proximity to the much-anticipated launch date isn't stemming the tide of leaks that has been plaguing the game for much of the past year. Yesterday, a new video - seemingly from a record store that received vinyl records of the soundtrack early - showed off the full 34-song tracklist for the game. Thanks to the listing printed on the back of Grand Theft Auto 6: The Album vinyl, we have a better idea of the licensed music that'll appear in-game. Travis Scott, Rina Sawayama, Cardi B, Pinkpantheress, SZA, Keith Richards, Dua Lipa, Jennie, Lana Del Rey, Zara Larsson are just some of the names that make up the impressive list. We know about a few of these tracks from September's announcement of the record , but only six tracks were revealed then, not the whole list. Take a look at the full track listing below: You can expect to hear these tracks on the radio - alongside many more, no doubt - and deployed at curated times during cutscenes or in missions, to really tie together the vibe of the city. This is something Vice City did remarkably well its roster of 80s tracks, and I can't wait to see how Rockstar has used more contemporary music in the same way here. Of course, there have been a lot of Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks in the run-up to the game's launch. Another recent example is the full game's map which seemingly leaked online thanks to the £350 collector's edition on show in a UK department store. Then there were all the leaks from a group calling itself CyberLeek , which shared unofficial gameplay and map details over the course of a few weeks, before Rockstar had even revealed much gameplay itself. Amongst all this, Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees . The case's conclusion will be determined this week , as the game goes on sale.

O grande destaque desta vez não poderia ser outro além de Grand Theft Auto VI , o novo jogo de mundo aberto da Rockstar Games ambientado em Vice City, que promete ser um dos títulos mais vendidos da história. Outro destaque é Spirit Crossing . O game cooperativo permite que você se junte a outros jogadores para povoar vilas, decorando casas e seus ambientes, em uma jogabilidade divertida e aconchegante. Confira a lista completa de lançamentos da semana e seus preços. Motocross The Game é um simulador de corrida que busca reproduzir a física do esporte sobre duas rodas. No game, a motocicleta e o piloto funcionam como corpos físicos separados, exigindo que o jogador controle a transferência de peso, o acelerador, a embreagem e a inclinação no ar para encarar diferentes tipos de terreno e pistas. O título chega em acesso antecipado para PC e conta com modos para um jogador e partidas multiplayer online em servidores dedicados. Além de permitir personalizar os equipamentos do piloto e os gráficos da moto, o game inclui assistências ajustáveis para iniciantes e rankings globais de contra-relógio. O jogo ainda não tem preço definido no Brasil. Spirit Crossing é um jogo multiplayer online desenvolvido pela Spry Fox, estúdio responsável por títulos como Cozy Grove . Ambientada na região conhecida como Crosslands, a experiência foca na cooperação entre jogadores para construir e decorar tanto casas próprias quanto espaços comunitários compartilhados pelo mapa. Durante a exploração, os jogadores interagem com habitantes locais, incluindo humanos, ursos falantes e espíritos. É preciso ajudá-los a resolver tarefas e acompanhar o desenvolvimento de suas histórias ao longo do tempo. O título aposta em uma abordagem voltada para a convivência e o progresso gradual, sem foco em combate. O game ainda não tem preço definido Depois de 13 anos de espera, GTA 6 será finalmente lançado. O novo jogo de ação e aventura em mundo aberto da Rockstar Games marca o retorno da franquia para o estado de Leonida e as ruas de Vice City. A história acompanha a dupla de protagonistas Lucia Caminos e Jason Duval em uma trama que envolve assaltos, perseguições e atividades criminosas pela região. Além de expandir a escala do mapa e a quantidade de atividades paralelas disponíveis para exploração, o título apresenta melhorias técnicas voltadas para os consoles da atual geração.
